tasks.short: Visit work sites, assess traffic impacts and document recommended control measures.

steps.what: Retrieve development plans, traffic control drawings and site safety requirements
Travel to the development or work site and obtain safe access
Inspect traffic movements, control measures and safety conditions at the site
Record site observations, locations and evidence of traffic control deficiencies
Assess projects' traffic effects and the adequacy of control and safety plans
Write the suggested traffic control measures and their site-specific reasons
Send the checked site recommendations to the directing traffic engineer

tasks.design: Configure linked site plans and observation headings in {DOCS}, with project references in {PROJECT}. Keep travel, inspection and assessment, separately write the recommendation, and send its checked final version to the engineer through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans, site observations and recommendation wording are repeatedly assembled.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document views and site templates can reduce supporting preparation and recording.
tasks.still_hard: The live traffic situation and changing work layout require on-site assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsafe arrangements and suggest practical, site-specific measures.
tasks.altitude: Put more attention on observed traffic risk than repeated document navigation.

reach.learn: Connect recommendations to current observations and plan versions.

evidence.claim: Native site views and observation templates could shorten supporting recording and lookup; they do not assess the adequacy of live traffic controls.

assumptions: This task includes the observation record, written recommendation and internal engineer send, each separately priced from the site visit.

The technician produces site, time, location, observed movement, deficiency and evidence references in s4, retaining 10.5 hours. Missing or stale plans require manual clarification; no machine safety verdict consumes the entries.
Native links and headings precede custom software. Internal authoring and saves have no self-approval stage; the actual send checks its exact final content and colleague recipient.
unknowns: Availability of current site drawings and existing observation templates.
research_questions: Does a native site record reduce preparation and writing without obscuring changes since the drawing was issued?

already_counted.description: Capture site observations and evidence references.

incremental.description: Maintain site headings and reference links.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final site recommendations, observations and engineer recipient; edits or recipient changes require a fresh send-time check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=92.5, gross=7.5; upkeep=1.5 gives net=6. Conservative case: outdated drawings require full lookup and bespoke recommendation writing; observation headings save only 1.5 hours, R=98.5, net=0. With usable headings, lookup at nine hours, observations at 12 and recommendation writing at 4.5 give R=95.5 and net=3. Travel, inspection, assessment and sending retain 70 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate traffic counters and record verified volume, class and movement observations.

steps.what: Define the specified traffic observation times, movements and counting categories
Set up counters and check their operation at the observation location
Record the counter session, location, time intervals and movement definitions
Operate counters and observe vehicular or pedestrian movements during specified intervals
Record count data, traffic type, movement and any disturbed intervals
Check count records for missing intervals and incorrect movement labels

tasks.design: Configure a native traffic count entry layout in {SPREADSHEET}, linked to the session definitions in {DOCS}. Retain counter setup and operation, context capture and record checks; simplify only the separate count entry action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings and movement labels are repeatedly written into ad hoc session sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: A native entry layout can reuse the session headings and category choices.
tasks.still_hard: Equipment faults, unusual movements and disturbed intervals require field judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Know when a count interval is not representative or reliable.
tasks.altitude: Improve count provenance while preserving field observation.

reach.learn: Interpret interval coverage and disturbance notes.

evidence.claim: Native count-entry headings and category choices could reduce manual recording without replacing counter operation.

assumptions: Counter measurement is existing equipment functionality, so no new saving is attributed to automatic sensing. Manual operation remains fully retained.

The technician produces session ID, site, interval boundaries, movement and class definitions in s3 with all 10 hours counted, then records readings and disturbances in s5 with nine retained hours. Missing or ambiguous readings require manual clarification or a repeat interval.
The layout provides headings and category choices; it does not hide an import, generated alert or machine record write. Native settings come first.
This task owns the original session record; cross-source coding and loading to the analysis system belong to the compilation task. Same-system saves earn no additional saving.
unknowns: Counter output format and variation in movement categories.
research_questions: Can a native count layout shorten entry without masking missing or disturbed intervals?

already_counted.description: Record readings and disturbances with session context.

incremental.description: Maintain count category layouts and session guidance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=94, gross=6; upkeep=2 gives net=4. Conservative case: mixed pedestrian movements require bespoke labels and recording retains 13 of 15 hours; R=98, net=0. Standard categories retaining 11 entry hours give R=96 and net=2. Setup, metadata, actual operation and checks retain 85 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure vehicle speeds and separately record their measurement context and quality.

steps.what: Position and check the electrical timing devices or radar equipment
Record speed session location, equipment identity, units and measurement conditions
Measure vehicular traffic speed and identify unreliable readings
Record measured speeds, observation times and measurement quality notes
Verify the speed record's units, timing and invalid-reading annotations

tasks.design: Use a native speed-entry layout in {SPREADSHEET}, with session instructions in {DOCS}. Keep positioning, equipment checks and actual measurement with the technician; reduce repeated entry of units, session headings and quality labels in the separate record step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Speed readings are entered alongside repeatedly written measurement context.
tasks.enabler_now: A native session layout can reuse fixed headings and quality categories.
tasks.still_hard: Target selection, positioning and unreliable returns require field attention.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the reading does not represent a valid vehicle measurement.
tasks.altitude: Produce clearer speed records without changing field judgement.

reach.learn: Check units, sample context and rejected observations.

evidence.claim: Native speed-entry headings and quality categories could reduce recording effort; existing radar measurement is not a new automation gain.

assumptions: No new automatic sensing or device export is proposed. The technician retains all measurement and equipment setup time.

The technician produces location, equipment ID, units, time basis and conditions in s2 with all 10 hours counted, then enters each reading and invalidity note in s4 with 12 retained hours. Ambiguous readings are manually checked or repeated.
The native layout offers reusable fields without a hidden machine transfer. Cross-source compilation belongs to the compilation task; original recording is priced here.
Ordinary same-system saves remain incidental and ungated, with no separate saving.
unknowns: Current device display format and proportion of invalid or unusual readings.
research_questions: Does the native layout reduce recording time when units and quality notes vary between devices?

already_counted.description: Record measured speeds and quality annotations.

incremental.description: Maintain speed layouts and device-specific unit guidance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=92, gross=8; upkeep=2 gives net=6. Conservative case: incompatible device units and frequent quality notes retain 18 of 20 entry hours; R=98, net=0. Stable units and routine measurements retaining 14 entry hours give R=94 and net=4. Setup, session capture, actual measurement and checking retain 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile count and speed records, code their fields and load a checked analysis dataset.

steps.what: Gather hand count sheets, machine count tapes and radar speed records
Capture source values and define their coding and interval mappings
Code traffic classes, directions, intervals and speed units for computer input
Compile coded traffic rows into the required study input file
Check the compiled data against source totals, units and missing intervals
Load the checked final file into the separate traffic analysis system

tasks.design: Use native source views and field mappings in {SPREADSHEET} to code and compile records, then import the checked file into {DATA_PLATFORM}, the separate traffic analysis store. Keep digitising ambiguous source material, mapping capture and source reconciliation with the technician; gate the actual cross-system dataset load on its final file.
tasks.previous_blocker: Count and speed records use different classes, intervals and units and are repeatedly coded for analysis input.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed field mappings and native file imports can replace repeat coding and re-keying.
tasks.still_hard: Illegible sheets, inconsistent interval definitions and missing metadata need manual resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether source records are comparable enough to combine.

ambition.what: Identify incompatible intervals before traffic analysis starts.

tasks.altitude: Shift compilation effort toward comparability and source integrity.

reach.learn: Inspect source coverage and mapping exceptions.

evidence.claim: Deterministic field mapping and native imports could replace repeated traffic coding and second-system re-keying; this is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: This task owns cross-source compilation and a real load to a second analysis system. The original counter or speed session records are produced in their measurement tasks and are not credited again.

The technician produces digitised values, source ID, site, interval boundaries, movement class, direction, units and target mapping in s2, retaining all 20 hours, including manual entry from paper. Unreadable or unmapped values stop coding and require manual resolution.
Native mappings and imports precede custom code. Compilation writes only a draft input file; the final dataset load is a distinct gated action, unlike an ordinary same-system author save.
The technician checks final rows, source totals, units, coverage and target study in s5. Changes to the file or destination invalidate that load approval.
unknowns: Source format comparability and the analysis system's supported import schema.
research_questions: How much manual work remains when source intervals or classification schemes cannot be mapped directly?

already_counted.description: Digitise sources and capture field and interval mappings.

incremental.description: Maintain coding mappings, import checks and source exception handling.

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked study input file, row set, units, source coverage and target study; any file or destination change requires a fresh s5 check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central E1 case: B=100, R=47, gross=53; upkeep=8 gives net=45. Conservative case: legacy paper and incompatible codes retain 15 collection, 20 capture, 20 coding, nine compilation, 15 verification and five manual load hours; R=84, net=8. Compatible interval metadata with collection at 12, capture 20, coding 10, compilation zero, verification 15 and manual load five gives R=62, net=30. Neither case claims a benefit from a same-system save.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain field observation and traffic judgement while simplifying complete, traceable records and analysis input.
reach: Connect measured traffic conditions with source-comparable datasets and practical control recommendations.
role.ambitious_version: A traffic technician who observes safely and produces clear site recommendations and trustworthy analysis datasets.
